item.title: Treasurer tables supplementary budget
item.description: Treasurer Ian Ling-Stuckey, this afternoon, handed down and tabled the supplementary budget in Parliament. The money plan caters for allocations to respond to El Nino disaster, maintain fuel subsidy and preparation for 2027 national election among others.
item.content:encoded:
Treasurer Ian Ling-Stuckey, this afternoon, handed down and tabled the supplementary budget in Parliament.

The money plan caters for allocations to respond to El Nino disaster, maintain fuel subsidy and preparation for 2027 national election among others.

The supplementary sees the highest allocation of K1.1 billion towards fuel relief as part of the household assistance package, K500 million for El Nino, an additional K150 million to election preparations, and over K50 million extra for police and defence.

Treasurer Ling-Stuckey says this supplementary budget includes major reallocation and cuts.

Revenues and Expenditures are expected to go up by K1.3 billion, with the budget deficit remaining at K1.6 billion kina

The Supplementary budget, while generally welcomed by both sides of the house, was also heavily criticized.

Members raised issues about the cuts, reallocation and hidden costs in the money plan.

This was after Treasurer Ian Ling-Stuckey tabled the mini money plan.

Western Province Governor Taboi Awi Yoto was not in support of the budget to take money out of provinces.

East Sepik Governor Allan Bird queried the operational and capital expenditures.

Madang Mp Brian Kramer also queried the budget, stating it is not detailed.

The government's mini money is focused on El Nino, fuel subsidy, and preparation for the 2027 national election, among others.

item.title: PNG Power scrutinised
item.description: The persistent power outages throughout the country and the operations of PNG Power Limited were the subject of scrutiny today in Parliament. Abau MP Sir Puka Temu raised questions about the state entity described and acknowledged by Government as a terminally ill patient.
item.content:encoded:
The persistent power outages throughout the country and the operations of PNG Power Limited were the subject of scrutiny today in Parliament.

Abau MP Sir Puka Temu raised questions about the state entity described and acknowledged by Government as a terminally ill patient.

He queried what its doing to save PNG Power Limited.

Abau MP Sir Puka Temu described the power situation in the country and that of PNG Power as a very sad one.

Minister in charge of PNG Power Richard Maru outlined his plans including a submission to the National Executive Council for the repayment of K100 million of the K200 million owed by Government.

He also proposed the sale of PNG Powers B and C centers or its small non profitable power hubs across the country.

Port Moresby, Ramu and Gazelle power grids are the only profitable grids at present.

Maru acknowledged PNG Powers debts of K1.3 billion, adding its revenue of K86 million per month is sufficient to keep the power company afloat.

Minister Maru is hopeful of getting PNG Power back on its feet before elections in 2027.

item.title: State power company could be operating illegally
item.description: Sinesine Yongomugl MP Kerenga Kua told Parliament today, PNG Power Limited could be operating illegally if its unable to pay its debts, calling the power company insolvent. Kua highlighted its a crime under the Companies Act.
item.content:encoded:
Sinesine Yongomugl MP Kerenga Kua told Parliament today, PNG Power Limited could be operating illegally if its unable to pay its debts, calling the power company insolvent.

Kua highlighted its a crime under the Companies Act.

In a supplementary question today in Parliament, Kua queried the legality of the state power company.

However this was interrupted by a point of order by Prime Minister James Marape.

An adamant Maru reiterated that PNG Power is meeting its daily operational costs and while has outstanding, has to just pay them off.

Apart from owing stakeholders K1.3 billion in debt, it's owed K200 million by Government.

item.title: Bougainville patriotism day
item.description: A public holiday is being observed across the Autonomous Region of Bougainville today to mark the Bougainville Patriotism Day. The Patriotic Day reinforces unity and reminds Bougainvilleans about their long history of struggle for independence, which predates that of mainland Papua New Guinea.
item.content:encoded:
A public holiday is being observed across the Autonomous Region of Bougainville today to mark the Bougainville Patriotism Day.

The Patriotic Day reinforces unity and reminds Bougainvilleans about their long history of struggle for independence, which predates that of mainland Papua New Guinea.

This year’s commemorations are being held across the region’s main towns of Buka for North Bougainville, Arawa for Central and Buin for South Bougainville under the theme: ‘Bougainville Patriots: United for Independence.

A vehicle float across Buka Town, march-in by school children, flags on proud display and a ceremonial parade by the Bougainville Police Service, marked commemorations at the Hutjena Oval.

The Bougainville Police Service was supported by their Correctional Service counterpart, in a parade of pride and discipline.

Government leaders, departments and agencies and the public converged at Hutjena to join the celebrations.

As the future of Bougainville rests before the National Legislature for a final determination, Minister for Infrastructure and Utilities, Patrick Nisira says history must not only be remembered but must also shape the future of the region.

Patriotism Day commemorates Bougainville’s 1975 declaration of independence, a fortnight before Papua New Guinea attained independence from Australia.

It honours the region’s struggle for self-determination, the Bougainville Peace Agreement and the overwhelming 97-point-7 YES vote in the 2019 Referendum on Independence.

This year’s event carries added weight as Bougainville moves towards its targeted date for self-government in 2027 and proposed independence in 2030.

President Ishmael Toroama delivered the keynote address in Arawa and Vice President Ezekiel Masatt addressed the people in Buin in similar commemorations, reflecting on history, reaffirming peace and strengthening the call for independence.

item.title: Health Minister calls for stronger PHAs
item.description: Health Minister, Dr. Billy Joseph is calling for stronger Provincial Health Authorities (PHA), greater accountability and better health outcomes as PNG marks 20 years of PHA reforms. Dr Billy Joseph made the call while officially opening the 60th Papua New Guinea Medical Symposium at the PNG University of Technology in Lae this week.
item.content:encoded:
Health Minister, Dr. Billy Joseph is calling for stronger Provincial Health Authorities (PHA), greater accountability and better health outcomes as PNG marks 20 years of PHA reforms.

Dr Billy Joseph made the call while officially opening the 60th Papua New Guinea Medical Symposium at the PNG University of Technology in Lae this week.

The theme is “Provincial Health Authorities Establishment Review: Past, Present and Future — PHAs Forward and Back.”

He says PNG now has more health facilities, health workers and investment which has grown from K346 million in 2007 to more than K3.2 billion in 2026, but key health indicators have not improved at the same pace.

Dr Joseph said skilled births remain at 44 percent, routine immunization is below 50 percent for some vaccines, tuberculosis (TB) rates are above 400 per 100,000, and around 1,256 health facilities remain closed.

He outlined a 120-Day Plan with 10 priorities including stronger leadership, medical supply reform, health infrastructure, workforce strengthening and a national pre-hospital care system.

The Minister stressed that PHA Boards and CEOs must be held accountable, with performance measured by results delivered to patients and communities.

Dr Joseph said the PHA review must lead to action to build a stronger, more accountable health system for the next 50 years of PNG.

item.title: Teachers bear brunt of Madang El Nino crisis
item.description: Teachers and their families in Madang are bearing the brunt of the worsening El Niño-induced dry spell as schools across the province struggle to operate without basic water supplies and an official provincial action plan. The Teaching Service Commission [TSC] in Madang has raised serious concerns over the welfare of educators, stating that prolonged heat and severe water shortages in rural school
item.content:encoded:
Teachers and their families in Madang are bearing the brunt of the worsening El Niño-induced dry spell as schools across the province struggle to operate without basic water supplies and an official provincial action plan.

The Teaching Service Commission [TSC] in Madang has raised serious concerns over the welfare of educators, stating that prolonged heat and severe water shortages in rural schools are threatening both lives and learning.

Acting Provincial TSC Advisor Kenneth Kalai expressed deep concern for non-local teachers posted to remote areas who are currently struggling for basic survival.

"I am particularly concerned about my teachers and their families. Most of them are not from the local communities," Kalai said.

"Some of the schools they are teaching in, especially those in the rural areas, do not have water catchments. They use creeks and rivers to source their supply of water, and some of these water sources have dried up."

Kalai revealed that teachers are being forced to walk long distances to cart water for basic household and daily needs. The hardship has been compounded by rising local tensions over dwindling natural reserves.

"My concern is about the welfare of my teachers and their families because some local people are now restricting them from accessing the water sources. They are even charging them fees," he said.

Despite a meeting held by the Madang Provincial Education Board last month to address the crisis, local school administrators report a lack of clear directives from provincial authorities.

"The heat is unbearable, and the least the province should do is come up with a disaster management plan," Kalai said. "The silence in the province is deafening. Responsible authorities are not talking about El Niño."

In the absence of a provincial relief framework, the provincial education director has directed head teachers across Madang to monitor conditions daily and submit weekly situational reports.

Taking early emergency measures, the Madang Inspectorate approved temporary schedule changes for schools in Zones 2 and 3, covering the Ambenob and Transgogol local level government [LLG] areas.

While applauding the inspectorate’s proactive stance to protect staff and students from heat exhaustion, Kalai urged all provincial stakeholders to take immediate structural action before the situation turns fatal.

"We can't wait until someone dies," Kalai said.

item.title: Brothers complete 3500km walk across PNG for children with cancer
item.description: 130-day journey from Bougainville to Vanimo to fund hospital. Two brothers, Mel-Kizenderk and Kormson Nili, have walked 3,500 kilometers across half of Papua New Guinea to raise funds and awareness for children living with cancer.
item.content:encoded:
130-day journey from Bougainville to Vanimo to fund hospital.

Two brothers, Mel-Kizenderk and Kormson Nili, have walked 3,500 kilometers across half of Papua New Guinea to raise funds and awareness for children living with cancer.

The walk began in Bougainville on 14th November 2025 and ended 130 days later on 27th August 2026 at the Wutung Border Post in Vanimo, West Sepik.

Hailing from East New Britain and Enga, the brothers took on the challenge to address child cancer, a growing health concern in PNG.

According to the World Health Organisation, approximately 140 children are diagnosed with cancer every year in Papua New Guinea. WHO estimates the real number could be 400 or more, based on the country’s youth population.

At the Children’s Cancer Ward at Port Moresby General Hospital, there are only 12 beds to serve children since the ward opened in 2015.

“1000 children every year is not a small imaginary number, and with 12 beds in POMGEN, the numbers are alarming. This is based on global WHO averages from 200 other countries. Our country does not have reliable data, not even for census to begin with,” Mel said.

At every stop in communities, markets, schools and churches, the brothers shared messages on cancer signs, possible causes, and prevention, hoping to save at least one life.

Through the walk they also saw the urgent need for better health facilities in remote areas.

“It is the rural areas that are most difficult to reach. Main reasons being lack of education, language barriers and strong superstitious beliefs. This could be the main reason most children in those areas are suffering and dying from cancer, but the data is not being collected,” Mel said.

The brothers say they hope to bring to the attention of every citizen in PNG, especially leaders, that this long-neglected disease is killing thousands of children across the country’s 22 provinces.

“We walk so more children can get a bed. We walk so more lives can be saved,” he said.

All funds raised through their 'Walk for Kids with Cancer' GoFundMe page will be used to purchase more beds and medication for the children’s cancer.

item.title: Call for peace at Koroba secondary school ahead of national examinations
item.description: Teachers and students of Koroba Secondary have been called on to reconcile, forgive one another and unite in restoring peace at the school ahead of the Grade 10 and 12 National Examinations next month. Hela Provincial Administrator Ronny Angu urged the students when he visited the school on Monday, 31st August to address a recent student strike and concerns raised by the school community.
item.content:encoded:
Teachers and students of Koroba Secondary have been called on to reconcile, forgive one another and unite in restoring peace at the school ahead of the Grade 10 and 12 National Examinations next month.

Hela Provincial Administrator Ronny Angu urged the students when he visited the school on Monday, 31st August to address a recent student strike and concerns raised by the school community.

As part of efforts to support the reconciliation process, Angu presented K10,000 to the school to prepare a special meal for students and teachers to share after the reconciliation ceremony.

“Students are our future. We cannot allow them to sit for their examinations without peace being restored. This reconciliation is important so our children can concentrate on their studies and perform well,” he said.

The PA also announced K40,000 in funding to provide meals for students throughout the examination period.

Meanwhile, the lack of reliable electricity has been identified as another major challenge affecting the school. To address the issue, Angu presented K100,000 to support the purchase of a new generator set.

“Our concern is you, the students. All we want from you is to focus on your education and make us proud by achieving top marks and gaining entry into tertiary institutions,” he said.

School Principal Stanley Langap thanked the Hela Provincial Government for the timely intervention, saying the assistance would help create a stable, peaceful and conducive learning environment for students as they prepare to sit their national examinations.

The school community is now expected to work together to restore harmony and ensure students can approach their examinations with peace of mind and confidence.
